title: Ready for the Interview

lines.text: Hi Dan, it's Nora. I heard you have a job interview on Thursday.
That's right, at a travel agency. I'm really nervous. Any advice?
First, you should research the company. If you know what they do, you'll sound more confident.
Good idea. I've already read their website, but I haven't looked at their social media.
You ought to do that too. They post photos of their trips every week.
What about clothes? Do I need to wear a suit?
Not necessarily. If it's a small office, a clean shirt and trousers will be fine.
Okay. And what if they ask about my weaknesses?
Be honest, but explain how you're working on them. You could say you used to be late, but now you leave home earlier.
That's clever. Should I bring a copy of my CV?
Yes, and bring a notebook as well. If you take notes, they'll see you're really interested.
Thanks, Nora. If I get the job, I'll invite you to dinner!

title: A New Library Card

Of course. Have you ever been a member of this library before?
No, I've lived in this city for only three months.
Welcome, then. I need some identification. Have you brought your passport?
I haven't brought my passport, but I have my student card. Is that okay?
That's fine. And an address, please.
I've been staying with my aunt since September. I can show you a letter from the university.
Perfect. You can borrow up to six books for three weeks. If you keep them longer, you'll pay a small fine.
How much is the fine?
It's twenty pence a day for each book. You can also renew books online.
Great. Have the new science fiction novels arrived yet?

title: Walls That Talk

lines.text: Welcome to Urban Walks. I'm Ellie, and today we're talking about street art.
And I'm Raj. Ellie, I used to think street art was just graffiti, but I've changed my mind.
Me too. In many cities now, artists are paid by councils to paint big murals on old walls.
That's true. In my neighbourhood, a huge picture of a fox was painted last summer on the side of a car park.
Who painted it?
A woman who studied art in Lisbon. It took her two weeks, and the paint was donated by a local shop.
Nice. And what do people think?
Most neighbours love it. Before the mural, the wall was covered with ugly marks. Now tourists take photos of it all the time.
Is it legal to paint anywhere?
No, you need permission. If you paint without it, you could get a fine.
So the lesson is: ask first, then create!
Exactly. Next week, we'll visit a market where a street artist sells small paintings.

lines.text: Good afternoon. How can I help you?
My suitcase didn't arrive. I was waiting at the carousel for an hour, but it never came.
I'm sorry about that. What flight were you on?
I was on the flight from Madrid. We landed at about two o'clock.
Can you describe your suitcase?
It's a large blue one with a yellow ribbon on the handle. I was wearing a red scarf when I checked in, if that helps.
It doesn't, but thanks. Did you put your name on the bag?
Yes, and my phone number. Inside there are some clothes, a camera and my medicine.
Don't worry. We'll try to find it. If it's still in Madrid, it'll arrive on tomorrow's first flight.
Will someone deliver it to my hotel?
Yes. Give me the name of your hotel, and we'll bring it as soon as it arrives.
It's the Hotel Marina, near the harbour. Thank you so much.

title: Join Green Hands
focus: Modals of obligation; infinitive of purpose

lines.text: Are you looking for a way to meet new people and help your community? Then come and join Green Hands.
We're a group of volunteers who clean parks and plant trees in the north of the city.
You don't have to be an expert. You just need to bring gloves and a bottle of water.
We meet every Saturday at nine in the morning at the gate of Riverside Park.
Everyone must wear comfortable shoes, because we sometimes walk a long way.
Children under twelve can't take part unless an adult comes with them.
At eleven we stop to have a snack, and the group leader brings fruit and juice for everyone.
Last month, we planted fifty trees, and we're hoping to plant more this spring.
You don't need to pay anything to join. Just write to us through our website.
Come and see how much fun it can be to make a difference!

title: The Water Filter Project

lines.text: Today we're at the school science fair, and I'm talking to Omar, who built a water filter. Omar, tell us about your project.
Well, my grandmother lives in a village where the water isn't always clean, so I wanted to find a cheap way to filter it.
How does your filter work?
It has three layers: sand, small stones and charcoal. The water goes through them slowly, and the dirt stays at the top.
Did it work the first time?
No, it didn't. Although I followed the instructions, the water was still cloudy. Then I realised I had used the wrong kind of sand.
So what did you do?
I washed the sand and tried again. This time the water looked much clearer.
Is it safe to drink?
Not yet. My teacher says we need to boil it first, because the filter can't remove every germ.
Will you keep improving it?
Yes, and next year I want to send a model to my grandmother's village.

title: Arriving After Midnight

lines.text: Good evening, Hotel Alba. Oliver speaking.
Hello, I have a reservation for tonight under the name Mei Tanaka. My plane has been delayed, so I won't arrive before midnight.
Don't worry, Miss Tanaka. Reception is open all night. Could you tell me when your flight lands?
It lands at ten forty, but then I'll need a taxi, so I'll probably get there at half past eleven.
That's fine. If you arrive after midnight, just ring the bell, and someone will let you in.
Thanks. Also, would it be possible to have a room on a quiet floor? I have a meeting early tomorrow.
Let me check. Yes, we can give you a room on the fourth floor, at the back of the building. It faces the garden.
Wonderful. Is breakfast included?
It is. It's served from seven until ten, but if you need to leave earlier, we can prepare a packed breakfast.
That would be great. Could I have it at six thirty?
Of course. I'll leave it at reception for you. Safe travels, Miss Tanaka.
